To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single-chip ultrasonic fingerprint sensor was developed that uses transmit beamforming to improve the image quality and contrast of the captured image.
a $65 \times42$  ultrasonic pulse-echosensor with TX beamforming has been developed.

we present a single chip  $65 \text{ } \times \text{ } 42$  piezoelectric ultrasonic fingerprint sensor with transmit beamforming, that is fabricated on CMOS, with a 6.4 times narrower beam width and a 1.5 times higher image contrast than a non beamformed sensor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of fingerprint sensors based on the use of a single-chip ultrasonic sensor array, which is fabricated in a standard CMOS technology.
the development of ultrasonic pulse- echo fingerprint sensors based on piezomicroelectromechanical systems (piezomicroelectrical mechanical systems) (piezomEMS).
the development of an ultrasonic pulse-echosensor for fingerprint identification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper demonstrates the first single-chip ultrasonic fingerprint sensor that is based on a PMUT array bonded to a CMO S readout ASIC and that the use of TX beamforming increases image quality.

this work presents a single-chip, ultrasonic pulse- echo fingerprint sensor that uses TX beamforming to improve image contrast, and that is fabricated in a standard  180-nm, 24-V CMOS process with an ASIC that includes a  $65 \cdot 42$  array of PMUTs.
this work demonstrates a single-chip ultrasonic pulse- echo fingerprint sensor that can be used for high-quality fingerprint imaging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a CMOS ultrasonic pulse- echo fingerprint sensor with TX beamforming that has the potential to be integrated into a smartphone.
we have successfully developed a single-chip ultrasonic fingerprint sensor with TX beamforming that is suitable for commercialization.
the sensor can provide an image contrast of  $0.2~\mu \mathrm{m}$, with a  $50~ \mu \text{ m}$  beamwidth, a frame rate of  $1~\text{Hz}$  and an image resolution of  $100 \times 65$  pixels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single-chip ultrasonic fingerprint sensor can be realized with TX beamforming using a PMUT array bonded to a CMOST readout ASIC.
the TX beamforming technique can be used to improve the performance of a fingerprint sensor by increasing the ultrasonic signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
a single-chip TX beamformer can be integrated with an ultrasonic sensor, enabling the development of low-cost, low-power, and high-performance ultrasonic fingerprint sensors.
